title: Human cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase (CYP7A1) deficiency has a hypercholesterolemic phenotype
authors: Pullinger CR, Eng C, Salen G, Shefer S, Batta AK, Erickson SK, et al.
population: One kindred of English and Celtic background with three homozygotes and six heterozygotes for a CYP7A1 deletion
funder: NIH grants HL-50782, HL-50779 and DK-26756; American Heart Association Western States Affiliates Grant-in-Aid 98-212 and National 0150571N; gifts from the Joseph Drown Foundation, the Donald T. and Rachel C. Valentine Foundation, Donald Yellon and Donald and Susan Schleicher; Department of Veterans Affairs merit awards; General Clinical Research Center funds from the National Center for Research Resources (5 MO1 RR-00079).
authorConflicts: No conflict of interest has been declared.
result: A homozygous deletion causing the frameshift L413fsX414 abolished CYP7A1 activity. The three homozygotes had average total cholesterol above 300 mg/dl and LDL cholesterol above 180 mg/dl. In one homozygote, hepatic cholesterol was double normal, faecal bile acid excretion was 6% of normal and CYP27A1 activity was doubled. The two male homozygotes had premature gallstone disease and LDL cholesterol resistant to HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors. Heterozygotes had age- and sex-adjusted LDL cholesterol 30 mg/dl higher than unaffected relatives.
